authority: Only validated append-only Security Incident events determine SEC identity, occurrence history, lifecycle, containment, remediation, security verification, and security-specific closure. Narrative prose, browser logic, an LLM recommendation, an Operational Incident, and the relationship journal are not Security Incident authority.
admission_boundary: Admit a credible suspected or confirmed security event, or a material security near miss, that requires investigation or containment. Routine alerts, ordinary hardening, stale reviews, intentional pause, and operational disruption without a security event do not enter this ledger solely because they exist.
recurrence: Repeated typed occurrences attach to one unresolved SEC. Recurrence after verified resolution creates a new SEC linked to the prior SEC without rewriting either history.
closure: Resolved is terminal and requires an exact closure test, result, disposition code, verifier, verified time, and one or more opaque restricted evidence references. Operational recovery never closes a Security Incident.
privacy: The event ledger stores only safe summaries, typed identities, and opaque restricted evidence references. It rejects secret-shaped material and deny-by-default unknown fields. Detailed evidence remains in the separate owner-local restricted evidence authority and no usable credential or secret may enter the ledger.
allocation: SEC identifiers are allocated independently from INC identifiers and from every other project sequence.
